newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore "surprised" at Malaysian comment on ties.
newsitem.headline: Singapore "surprised" at Malaysian comment on ties.

text.p: Singapore said it was surprised at a statement by Malaysia that the relationship between the two countries, jarred by comments from Singapore Senior Minister Lee Kuan Yew, would take time to heal.

"The government of Singapore is surprised that the Malaysian government has stated that 'restoration of the old level of relationship would take time'," Singapore Foreign Affairs Minister Shanmugam Jayakumar said in a statement released late on Wednesday.

Malaysian Foreign Minister Abdullah Badawi told reporters on Wednesday Kuala Lumpur accepted Lee's apology for describing the south Malaysian state of Johor as "notorious for shootings, muggings and car-jackings" in a Singapore court affidavit.
Abdullah said after a cabinet meeting that Malaysia also viewed positively Lee's move to get the offending remarks deleted from the affidavit.
But he said: "However, it should be acknowledged that this episode has deeply hurt Malaysians of all sections of society and that restoration of the old level of relationship would take time."
Jayakumar said Singapore noted the statement accepting the apology. Lee's comments on Johor were made by him personally in a private capacity, Jayakumar said.

"The government of Singapore has always attached importance to its relations with Malaysia and will work with the Malaysian government to enhance this relationship. We believe that cooperation between the two countries can only result in a win-win situation," Jayakumar said.
